mismatch.wharton: thou shalt not defraud thy neighbour, neither rob him : the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning.

mismatch.clean: six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation; ye shall do no work therein: it is the sabbath of the lord in all your dwellings.
mismatch.wharton: six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation; ye shall do no work therein : it is the sabbath of the lord in all your dwellings.

mismatch.clean: ye shall do no servile work therein: but ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the lord.
mismatch.wharton: ye shall do no servile work therein : but ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the lord.

mismatch.wharton: and if thy brother be waxen poor, and fallen in decay with thee; then thou shalt relieve him: yea, though he be a stranger, or a sojourner; that he may live with thee.

mismatch.wharton: and the people journeyed from kibrothhattaavah unto hazeroth; and abode at hazeroth.

mismatch.clean: and the lord shall make thee the head, and not the tail; and thou shalt be above only, and thou shalt not be beneath; if that thou hearken unto the commandments of the lord thy god, which i command thee this day, to observe and to do them:

mismatch.wharton: thou shalt plant vineyards, and dress them , but shalt neither drink of the wine, nor gather the grapes ; for the worms shall eat them.

mismatch.clean: because thou servedst not the lord thy god with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things;

mismatch.clean: therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.

mismatch.clean: and it came to pass, as they fled from before israel, and were in the going down to beth-horon, that the lord cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto azekah, and they died: they were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of israel slew with the sword.
mismatch.wharton: and it came to pass, as they fled from before israel, and were in the going down to bethhoron, that the lord cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto azekah, and they died: they were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of israel slew with the sword.

mismatch.wharton: and joshua smote them from kadeshbarnea even unto gaza, and all the country of goshen, even unto gibeon.

mismatch.clean: and he answered, thou shalt not smite them: wouldest thou smite those whom thou hast taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow? set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, and go to their master.
mismatch.wharton: and he answered, thou shalt not smite them : wouldest thou smite those whom thou hast taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow? set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, and go to their master.

mismatch.clean: and it came to pass after this, that ben-hadad king of syria gathered all his host, and went up, and besieged samaria.
mismatch.wharton: and it came to pass after this, that benhadad king of syria gathered all his host, and went up, and besieged samaria.

mismatch.clean: and when these lepers came to the uttermost part of the camp, they went into one tent, and did eat and drink, and carried thence silver, and gold, and raiment, and went and hid it; and came again, and entered into another tent, and carried thence also , and went and hid it .

mismatch.clean: and elisha came to damascus; and ben-hadad the king of syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, the man of god is come hither.
mismatch.wharton: and elisha came to damascus; and benhadad the king of syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, the man of god is come hither.

mismatch.clean: so hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of damascus, forty camels burden, and came and stood before him, and said, thy son ben-hadad king of syria hath sent me to thee, saying, shall i recover of this disease?
mismatch.wharton: so hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of damascus, forty camels burden, and came and stood before him, and said, thy son benhadad king of syria hath sent me to thee, saying, shall i recover of this disease?

mismatch.clean: and he went with joram the son of ahab to the war against hazael king of syria in ramoth-gilead; and the syrians wounded joram.
mismatch.wharton: and he went with joram the son of ahab to the war against hazael king of syria in ramothgilead; and the syrians wounded joram.

mismatch.clean: and elisha the prophet called one of the children of the prophets, and said unto him, gird up thy loins, and take this box of oil in thine hand, and go to ramoth-gilead:

mismatch.clean: so the young man, even the young man the prophet, went to ramoth-gilead.
mismatch.wharton: so the young man, even the young man the prophet, went to ramothgilead.

mismatch.clean: so jehu the son of jehoshaphat the son of nimshi conspired against joram. (now joram had kept ramoth-gilead, he and all israel, because of hazael king of syria.

mismatch.clean: and when jehu was come to jezreel, jezebel heard of it; and she painted her face, and tired her head, and looked out at a window.

mismatch.clean: howbeit from the sins of jeroboam the son of nebat, who made israel to sin, jehu departed not from after them, to wit , the golden calves that were in beth-el, and that were in dan.

mismatch.clean: in the seventh year of jehu jehoash began to reign; and forty years reigned he in jerusalem. and his mothers name was zibiah of beer-sheba.
mismatch.wharton: in the seventh year of jehu jehoash began to reign; and forty years reigned he in jerusalem. and his mothers name was zibiah of beersheba.

mismatch.clean: but it was so , that in the three and twentieth year of king jehoash the priests had not repaired the breaches of the house.

mismatch.clean: and the anger of the lord was kindled against israel, and he delivered them into the hand of hazael king of syria, and into the hand of ben-hadad the son of hazael, all their days.
mismatch.wharton: and the anger of the lord was kindled against israel, and he delivered them into the hand of hazael king of syria, and into the hand of benhadad the son of hazael, all their days.

mismatch.clean: and he said to the king of israel, put thine hand upon the bow. and he put his hand upon it: and elisha put his hands upon the kings hands.
mismatch.wharton: and he said to the king of israel, put thine hand upon the bow. and he put his hand upon it : and elisha put his hands upon the kings hands.

mismatch.clean: and the man of god was wroth with him, and said, thou shouldest have smitten five or six times; then hadst thou smitten syria till thou hadst consumed it: whereas now thou shalt smite syria but thrice.

mismatch.clean: and it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that, behold, they spied a band of men; and they cast the man into the sepulchre of elisha: and when the man was let down, and touched the bones of elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet.

mismatch.wharton: so hazael king of syria died; and benhadad his son reigned in his stead.

mismatch.clean: and jehoash the son of jehoahaz took again out of the hand of ben-hadad the son of hazael the cities, which he had taken out of the hand of jehoahaz his father by war. three times did joash beat him, and recovered the cities of israel.

mismatch.clean: but amaziah would not hear. therefore jehoash king of israel went up; and he and amaziah king of judah looked one another in the face at beth-shemesh, which belongeth to judah.
mismatch.wharton: but amaziah would not hear. therefore jehoash king of israel went up; and he and amaziah king of judah looked one another in the face at bethshemesh, which belongeth to judah.

mismatch.clean: and jehoash king of israel took amaziah king of judah, the son of jehoash the son of ahaziah, at beth-shemesh, and came to jerusalem, and brake down the wall of jerusalem from the gate of ephraim unto the corner gate, four hundred cubits.
mismatch.wharton: and jehoash king of israel took amaziah king of judah, the son of jehoash the son of ahaziah, at bethshemesh, and came to jerusalem, and brake down the wall of jerusalem from the gate of ephraim unto the corner gate, four hundred cubits.

mismatch.clean: he restored the coast of israel from the entering of hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the lord god of israel, which he spake by the hand of his servant jonah, the son of amittai, the prophet, which was of gath-hepher.

mismatch.clean: in the days of pekah king of israel came tiglath-pileser king of assyria, and took ijon, and abel-beth-maachah, and janoah, and kedesh, and hazor, and gilead, and galilee, all the land of naphtali, and carried them captive to assyria.

mismatch.clean: so ahaz sent messengers to tiglath-pileser king of assyria, saying, i am thy servant and thy son: come up, and save me out of the hand of the king of syria, and out of the hand of the king of israel, which rise up against me.

mismatch.clean: and king ahaz went to damascus to meet tiglath-pileser king of assyria, and saw an altar that was at damascus: and king ahaz sent to urijah the priest the fashion of the altar, and the pattern of it, according to all the workmanship thereof.
mismatch.wharton: and king ahaz went to damascus to meet tiglathpileser king of assyria, and saw an altar that was at damascus: and king ahaz sent to urijah the priest the fashion of the altar, and the pattern of it, according to all the workmanship thereof.

mismatch.clean: and the king of assyria sent tartan and rabsaris and rab-shakeh from lachish to king hezekiah with a great host against jerusalem. and they went up and came to jerusalem. and when they were come up, they came and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is in the highway of the fullers field.
mismatch.wharton: and the king of assyria sent tartan and rabsaris and rabshakeh from lachish to king hezekiah with a great host against jerusalem. and they went up and came to jerusalem. and when they were come up, they came and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is in the highway of the fullers field.

mismatch.clean: and rab-shakeh said unto them, speak ye now to hezekiah, thus saith the great king, the king of assyria, what confidence is this wherein thou trustest?
mismatch.wharton: and rabshakeh said unto them, speak ye now to hezekiah, thus saith the great king, the king of assyria, what confidence is this wherein thou trustest?

mismatch.clean: then said eliakim the son of hilkiah, and shebna, and joah, unto rab-shakeh, speak, i pray thee, to thy servants in the syrian language; for we understand it: and talk not with us in the jews language in the ears of the people that are on the wall.
mismatch.wharton: then said eliakim the son of hilkiah, and shebna, and joah, unto rabshakeh, speak, i pray thee, to thy servants in the syrian language; for we understand it : and talk not with us in the jews language in the ears of the people that are on the wall.

mismatch.clean: but rab-shakeh said unto them, hath my master sent me to thy master, and to thee, to speak these words? hath he not sent me to the men which sit on the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you?

mismatch.clean: then rab-shakeh stood and cried with a loud voice in the jews language, and spake, saying, hear the word of the great king, the king of assyria:
mismatch.wharton: then rabshakeh stood and cried with a loud voice in the jews language, and spake, saying, hear the word of the great king, the king of assyria:

mismatch.clean: then came eliakim the son of hilkiah, which was over the household, and shebna the scribe, and joah the son of asaph the recorder, to hezekiah with their clothes rent, and told him the words of rab-shakeh.
mismatch.wharton: then came eliakim the son of hilkiah, which was over the household, and shebna the scribe, and joah the son of asaph the recorder, to hezekiah with their clothes rent, and told him the words of rabshakeh.

mismatch.clean: it may be the lord thy god will hear all the words of rab-shakeh, whom the king of assyria his master hath sent to reproach the living god; and will reprove the words which the lord thy god hath heard: wherefore lift up thy prayer for the remnant that are left.
mismatch.wharton: it may be the lord thy god will hear all the words of rabshakeh, whom the king of assyria his master hath sent to reproach the living god; and will reprove the words which the lord thy god hath heard: wherefore lift up thy prayer for the remnant that are left.

mismatch.clean: so rab-shakeh returned, and found the king of assyria warring against libnah: for he had heard that he was departed from lachish.

mismatch.clean: manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and reigned fifty and five years in jerusalem. and his mothers name was hephzi-bah.
mismatch.wharton: manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and reigned fifty and five years in jerusalem. and his mothers name was hephzibah.

mismatch.clean: and the king commanded hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the door, to bring forth out of the temple of the lord all the vessels that were made for baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven: and he burned them without jerusalem in the fields of kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto beth-el.
mismatch.wharton: and the king commanded hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the door, to bring forth out of the temple of the lord all the vessels that were made for baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven: and he burned them without jerusalem in the fields of kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto bethel.

mismatch.clean: and he brought all the priests out of the cities of judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from geba to beer-sheba, and brake down the high places of the gates that were in the entering in of the gate of joshua the governor of the city, which were on a mans left hand at the gate of the city.

mismatch.clean: and he took away the horses that the kings of judah had given to the sun, at the entering in of the house of the lord, by the chamber of nathan-melech the chamberlain, which was in the suburbs, and burned the chariots of the sun with fire.

mismatch.clean: then he said, what title is that that i see? and the men of the city told him, it is the sepulchre of the man of god, which came from judah, and proclaimed these things that thou hast done against the altar of beth-el.

mismatch.clean: and all the houses also of the high places that were in the cities of samaria, which the kings of israel had made to provoke the lord to anger, josiah took away, and did to them according to all the acts that he had done in beth-el.
mismatch.wharton: and all the houses also of the high places that were in the cities of samaria, which the kings of israel had made to provoke the lord to anger, josiah took away, and did to them according to all the acts that he had done in bethel.

mismatch.clean: in his days pharaoh-nechoh king of egypt went up against the king of assyria to the river euphrates: and king josiah went against him; and he slew him at megiddo, when he had seen him.

mismatch.wharton: sing, o ye heavens; for the lord hath done it : shout, ye lower parts of the earth: break forth into singing, ye mountains, o forest, and every tree therein: for the lord hath redeemed jacob, and glorified himself in israel.

mismatch.clean: thus saith the lord, thy redeemer, and he that formed thee from the womb, i am the lord that maketh all things; that stretcheth forth the heavens alone; that spreadeth abroad the earth by myself;
mismatch.wharton: thus saith the lord, thy redeemer, and he that formed thee from the womb, i am the lord that maketh all things ; that stretcheth forth the heavens alone; that spreadeth abroad the earth by myself;

mismatch.clean: and even to your old age i am he; and even to hoar hairs will i carry you: i have made, and i will bear; even i will carry, and will deliver you .
mismatch.wharton: and even to your old age i am he; and even to hoar hairs will i carry you : i have made, and i will bear; even i will carry, and will deliver you .

mismatch.clean: thou hast heard, see all this; and will not ye declare it? i have shewed thee new things from this time, even hidden things, and thou didst not know them.
mismatch.wharton: thou hast heard, see all this; and will not ye declare it ? i have shewed thee new things from this time, even hidden things, and thou didst not know them.

mismatch.clean: for mine own sake, even for mine own sake, will i do it: for how should my name be polluted? and i will not give my glory unto another.
mismatch.wharton: for mine own sake, even for mine own sake, will i do it : for how should my name be polluted? and i will not give my glory unto another.

mismatch.clean: all ye, assemble yourselves, and hear; which among them hath declared these things? the lord hath loved him: he will do his pleasure on babylon, and his arm shall be on the chaldeans.
mismatch.wharton: all ye, assemble yourselves, and hear; which among them hath declared these things ? the lord hath loved him: he will do his pleasure on babylon, and his arm shall be on the chaldeans.

mismatch.clean: then shalt thou say in thine heart, who hath begotten me these, seeing i have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro? and who hath brought up these? behold, i was left alone; these, where had they been?
mismatch.wharton: then shalt thou say in thine heart, who hath begotten me these, seeing i have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro? and who hath brought up these? behold, i was left alone; these, where had they been ?

mismatch.clean: depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the lord.
mismatch.wharton: depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing ; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the lord.

mismatch.clean: when thou criest, let thy companies deliver thee; but the wind shall carry them all away; vanity shall take them: but he that putteth his trust in me shall possess the land, and shall inherit my holy mountain;
mismatch.wharton: when thou criest, let thy companies deliver thee; but the wind shall carry them all away; vanity shall take them : but he that putteth his trust in me shall possess the land, and shall inherit my holy mountain;

mismatch.clean: is it such a fast that i have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the lord?
mismatch.wharton: is it such a fast that i have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him ? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the lord?

mismatch.clean: thou shalt no more be termed forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed desolate: but thou shalt be called hephzi-bah, and thy land beulah: for the lord delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.
mismatch.wharton: thou shalt no more be termed forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed desolate: but thou shalt be called hephzibah, and thy land beulah: for the lord delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.

mismatch.clean: we are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name.
mismatch.wharton: we are thine : thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name.

mismatch.clean: i am sought of them that asked not for me; i am found of them that sought me not: i said, behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.
mismatch.wharton: i am sought of them that asked not for me ; i am found of them that sought me not: i said, behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.

mismatch.clean: and they shall build houses, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them.
mismatch.wharton: and they shall build houses, and inhabit them ; and they shall plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them.

mismatch.clean: shall i bring to the birth, and not cause to bring forth? saith the lord: shall i cause to bring forth, and shut the womb? saith thy god.
mismatch.wharton: shall i bring to the birth, and not cause to bring forth? saith the lord: shall i cause to bring forth, and shut the womb ? saith thy god.

mismatch.clean: is israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?
mismatch.wharton: is israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave ? why is he spoiled?

mismatch.clean: and it shall come to pass, when ye be multiplied and increased in the land, in those days, saith the lord, they shall say no more, the ark of the covenant of the lord: neither shall it come to mind: neither shall they remember it; neither shall they visit it; neither shall that be done any more.
mismatch.wharton: and it shall come to pass, when ye be multiplied and increased in the land, in those days, saith the lord, they shall say no more, the ark of the covenant of the lord: neither shall it come to mind: neither shall they remember it; neither shall they visit it ; neither shall that be done any more.

mismatch.clean: shall i not visit for these things? saith the lord: and shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
mismatch.wharton: shall i not visit for these things ? saith the lord: and shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?

mismatch.clean: for among my people are found wicked men: they lay wait, as he that setteth snares; they set a trap, they catch men.
mismatch.wharton: for among my people are found wicked men : they lay wait, as he that setteth snares; they set a trap, they catch men.

mismatch.clean: shall i not visit for these things? saith the lord: shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
mismatch.wharton: shall i not visit for these things ? saith the lord: shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?

mismatch.clean: o ye children of benjamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in tekoa, and set up a sign of fire in beth-haccerem: for evil appeareth out of the north, and great destruction.
mismatch.wharton: o ye children of benjamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in tekoa, and set up a sign of fire in bethhaccerem: for evil appeareth out of the north, and great destruction.

mismatch.clean: since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of egypt unto this day i have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them:
mismatch.wharton: since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of egypt unto this day i have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them :

mismatch.clean: how do ye say, we are wise, and the law of the lord is with us? lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain.
mismatch.wharton: how do ye say, we are wise, and the law of the lord is with us? lo, certainly in vain made he it ; the pen of the scribes is in vain.

mismatch.clean: therefore will i give their wives unto others, and their fields to them that shall inherit them: for every one from the least even unto the greatest is given to covetousness, from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely.
mismatch.wharton: therefore will i give their wives unto others, and their fields to them that shall inherit them : for every one from the least even unto the greatest is given to covetousness, from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely.

mismatch.clean: shall i not visit them for these things? saith the lord: shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?
mismatch.wharton: shall i not visit them for these things ? saith the lord: shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?

mismatch.clean: for the mountains will i take up a weeping and wailing, and for the habitations of the wilderness a lamentation, because they are burned up, so that none can pass through them; neither can men hear the voice of the cattle; both the fowl of the heavens and the beast are fled; they are gone.
mismatch.wharton: for the mountains will i take up a weeping and wailing, and for the habitations of the wilderness a lamentation, because they are burned up, so that none can pass through them ; neither can men hear the voice of the cattle; both the fowl of the heavens and the beast are fled; they are gone.

mismatch.clean: the portion of jacob is not like them: for he is the former of all things; and israel is the rod of his inheritance: the lord of hosts is his name.
mismatch.wharton: the portion of jacob is not like them: for he is the former of all things ; and israel is the rod of his inheritance: the lord of hosts is his name.

mismatch.clean: and the lord hath given me knowledge of it , and i know it: then thou shewedst me their doings.
mismatch.wharton: and the lord hath given me knowledge of it , and i know it : then thou shewedst me their doings.

mismatch.clean: the cities of the south shall be shut up, and none shall open them: judah shall be carried away captive all of it, it shall be wholly carried away captive.
mismatch.wharton: the cities of the south shall be shut up, and none shall open them : judah shall be carried away captive all of it, it shall be wholly carried away captive.

mismatch.clean: i have seen thine adulteries, and thy neighings, the lewdness of thy whoredom, and thine abominations on the hills in the fields. woe unto thee, o jerusalem! wilt thou not be made clean? when shall it once be?
mismatch.wharton: i have seen thine adulteries, and thy neighings, the lewdness of thy whoredom, and thine abominations on the hills in the fields. woe unto thee, o jerusalem! wilt thou not be made clean? when shall it once be ?

mismatch.clean: at what instant i shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to destroy it;
mismatch.wharton: at what instant i shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to destroy it ;

mismatch.clean: and at what instant i shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to build and to plant it;
mismatch.wharton: and at what instant i shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to build and to plant it ;

mismatch.clean: yet, lord, thou knowest all their counsel against me to slay me: forgive not their iniquity, neither blot out their sin from thy sight, but let them be overthrown before thee; deal thus with them in the time of thine anger.
mismatch.wharton: yet, lord, thou knowest all their counsel against me to slay me : forgive not their iniquity, neither blot out their sin from thy sight, but let them be overthrown before thee; deal thus with them in the time of thine anger.

mismatch.clean: and it came to pass on the morrow, that pashur brought forth jeremiah out of the stocks. then said jeremiah unto him, the lord hath not called thy name pashur, but magor-missabib.
mismatch.wharton: and it came to pass on the morrow, that pashur brought forth jeremiah out of the stocks. then said jeremiah unto him, the lord hath not called thy name pashur, but magormissabib.

mismatch.clean: for thus saith the lord, behold, i will make thee a terror to thyself, and to all thy friends: and they shall fall by the sword of their enemies, and thine eyes shall behold it: and i will give all judah into the hand of the king of babylon, and he shall carry them captive into babylon, and shall slay them with the sword.
mismatch.wharton: for thus saith the lord, behold, i will make thee a terror to thyself, and to all thy friends: and they shall fall by the sword of their enemies, and thine eyes shall behold it : and i will give all judah into the hand of the king of babylon, and he shall carry them captive into babylon, and shall slay them with the sword.

mismatch.clean: for who hath stood in the counsel of the lord, and hath perceived and heard his word? who hath marked his word, and heard it?
mismatch.wharton: for who hath stood in the counsel of the lord, and hath perceived and heard his word? who hath marked his word, and heard it ?

mismatch.clean: and the lord hath sent unto you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them; but ye have not hearkened, nor inclined your ear to hear.
mismatch.wharton: and the lord hath sent unto you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them ; but ye have not hearkened, nor inclined your ear to hear.

mismatch.clean: a voice of the cry of the shepherds, and an howling of the principal of the flock, shall be heard: for the lord hath spoiled their pasture.
mismatch.wharton: a voice of the cry of the shepherds, and an howling of the principal of the flock, shall be heard : for the lord hath spoiled their pasture.

mismatch.clean: and there was also a man that prophesied in the name of the lord, urijah the son of shemaiah of kirjath-jearim, who prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of jeremiah:
mismatch.wharton: and there was also a man that prophesied in the name of the lord, urijah the son of shemaiah of kirjathjearim, who prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of jeremiah:

mismatch.clean: build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them;
mismatch.wharton: build ye houses, and dwell in them ; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them;

mismatch.clean: because they have not hearkened to my words, saith the lord, which i sent unto them by my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them; but ye would not hear, saith the lord.
mismatch.wharton: because they have not hearkened to my words, saith the lord, which i sent unto them by my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them ; but ye would not hear, saith the lord.

mismatch.clean: for therefore he sent unto us in babylon, saying, this captivity is long: build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.
mismatch.wharton: for therefore he sent unto us in babylon, saying, this captivity is long: build ye houses, and dwell in them ; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.

mismatch.clean: i have surely heard ephraim bemoaning himself thus; thou hast chastised me, and i was chastised, as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke: turn thou me, and i shall be turned; for thou art the lord my god.
mismatch.wharton: i have surely heard ephraim bemoaning himself thus ; thou hast chastised me, and i was chastised, as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke : turn thou me, and i shall be turned; for thou art the lord my god.

mismatch.clean: neither shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any: but all your days ye shall dwell in tents; that ye may live many days in the land where ye be strangers.
mismatch.wharton: neither shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any : but all your days ye shall dwell in tents; that ye may live many days in the land where ye be strangers.

mismatch.clean: now when ebed-melech the ethiopian, one of the eunuchs which was in the kings house, heard that they had put jeremiah in the dungeon; the king then sitting in the gate of benjamin;
mismatch.wharton: now when ebedmelech the ethiopian, one of the eunuchs which was in the kings house, heard that they had put jeremiah in the dungeon; the king then sitting in the gate of benjamin;

mismatch.clean: ebed-melech went forth out of the kings house, and spake to the king, saying,
mismatch.wharton: ebedmelech went forth out of the kings house, and spake to the king, saying,

mismatch.clean: then the king commanded ebed-melech the ethiopian, saying, take from hence thirty men with thee, and take up jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon, before he die.
mismatch.wharton: then the king commanded ebedmelech the ethiopian, saying, take from hence thirty men with thee, and take up jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon, before he die.

mismatch.clean: so ebed-melech took the men with him, and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took thence old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to jeremiah.
mismatch.wharton: so ebedmelech took the men with him, and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took thence old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to jeremiah.

mismatch.clean: and ebed-melech the ethiopian said unto jeremiah, put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under thine armholes under the cords. and jeremiah did so.
mismatch.wharton: and ebedmelech the ethiopian said unto jeremiah, put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under thine armholes under the cords. and jeremiah did so.

mismatch.clean: and all the princes of the king of babylon came in, and sat in the middle gate, even nergal-sharezer, samgar-nebo, sarsechim, rab-saris, nergal-sharezer, rab-mag, with all the residue of the princes of the king of babylon.
mismatch.wharton: and all the princes of the king of babylon came in, and sat in the middle gate, even nergalsharezer, samgarnebo, sarsechim, rabsaris, nergalsharezer, rabmag, with all the residue of the princes of the king of babylon.

mismatch.clean: then nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carried away captive into babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to him, with the rest of the people that remained.
mismatch.wharton: then nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive into babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to him, with the rest of the people that remained.

mismatch.clean: but nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.
mismatch.wharton: but nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.

mismatch.clean: now nebuchadrezzar king of babylon gave charge concerning jeremiah to nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard, saying,
mismatch.wharton: now nebuchadrezzar king of babylon gave charge concerning jeremiah to nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, saying,

mismatch.clean: so nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard sent, and nebushasban, rab-saris, and nergal-sharezer, rab-mag, and all the king of babylons princes;
mismatch.wharton: so nebuzaradan the captain of the guard sent, and nebushasban, rabsaris, and nergalsharezer, rabmag, and all the king of babylons princes;

mismatch.clean: go and speak to ebed-melech the ethiopian, saying, thus saith the lord of hosts, the god of israel; behold, i will bring my words upon this city for evil, and not for good; and they shall be accomplished in that day before thee.
mismatch.wharton: go and speak to ebedmelech the ethiopian, saying, thus saith the lord of hosts, the god of israel; behold, i will bring my words upon this city for evil, and not for good; and they shall be accomplished in that day before thee.

mismatch.clean: the word that came to jeremiah from the lord, after that nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had let him go from ramah, when he had taken him being bound in chains among all that were carried away captive of jerusalem and judah, which were carried away captive unto babylon.

mismatch.clean: then johanan the son of kareah spake to gedaliah in mizpah secretly, saying, let me go, i pray thee, and i will slay ishmael the son of nethaniah, and no man shall know it: wherefore should he slay thee, that all the jews which are gathered unto thee should be scattered, and the remnant in judah perish?
mismatch.wharton: then johanan the son of kareah spake to gedaliah in mizpah secretly, saying, let me go, i pray thee, and i will slay ishmael the son of nethaniah, and no man shall know it : wherefore should he slay thee, that all the jews which are gathered unto thee should be scattered, and the remnant in judah perish?

mismatch.clean: then ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in mizpah, even the kings daughters, and all the people that remained in mizpah, whom nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had committed to gedaliah the son of ahikam: and ishmael the son of nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the ammonites.
mismatch.wharton: then ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in mizpah, even the kings daughters, and all the people that remained in mizpah, whom nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to gedaliah the son of ahikam: and ishmael the son of nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the ammonites.

mismatch.clean: and they departed, and dwelt in the habitation of chimham, which is by beth-lehem, to go to enter into egypt,

mismatch.clean: then jeremiah the prophet said unto them, i have heard you; behold, i will pray unto the lord your god according to your words; and it shall come to pass, that whatsoever thing the lord shall answer you, i will declare it unto you; i will keep nothing back from you.
mismatch.wharton: then jeremiah the prophet said unto them, i have heard you ; behold, i will pray unto the lord your god according to your words; and it shall come to pass, that whatsoever thing the lord shall answer you, i will declare it unto you; i will keep nothing back from you.

mismatch.clean: even men, and women, and children, and the kings daughters, and every person that nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard had left with gedaliah the son of ahikam the son of shaphan, and jeremiah the prophet, and baruch the son of neriah.
mismatch.wharton: even men, and women, and children, and the kings daughters, and every person that nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with gedaliah the son of ahikam the son of shaphan, and jeremiah the prophet, and baruch the son of neriah.

mismatch.clean: he shall break also the images of beth-shemesh, that is in the land of egypt; and the houses of the gods of the egyptians shall he burn with fire.
mismatch.wharton: he shall break also the images of bethshemesh, that is in the land of egypt; and the houses of the gods of the egyptians shall he burn with fire.

mismatch.clean: thus saith the lord; behold, i will give pharaoh-hophra king of egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as i gave zedekiah king of judah into the hand of nebuchadrezzar king of babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life.

mismatch.clean: against egypt, against the army of pharaoh-necho king of egypt, which was by the river euphrates in carchemish, which nebuchadrezzar king of babylon smote in the fourth year of jehoiakim the son of josiah king of judah.
mismatch.wharton: against egypt, against the army of pharaohnecho king of egypt, which was by the river euphrates in carchemish, which nebuchadrezzar king of babylon smote in the fourth year of jehoiakim the son of josiah king of judah.

mismatch.wharton: and upon dibon, and upon nebo, and upon bethdiblathaim,

mismatch.clean: and upon kiriathaim, and upon beth-gamul, and upon beth-meon,
mismatch.wharton: and upon kiriathaim, and upon bethgamul, and upon bethmeon,

mismatch.wharton: therefore will i howl for moab, and i will cry out for all moab; mine heart shall mourn for the men of kirheres.

mismatch.wharton: then said paul, i stand at caesars judgment seat, where i ought to be judged: to the jews have i done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.

mismatch.wharton: and now i exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any mans life among you, but of the ship.

mismatch.wharton: saying, fear not, paul; thou must be brought before caesar: and, lo, god hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

mismatch.wharton: for this cause therefore have i called for you, to see you , and to speak with you : because that for the hope of israel i am bound with this chain.

mismatch.wharton: and they said unto him, we neither received letters out of judaea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.

mismatch.wharton: what then? are we better than they ? no, in no wise: for we have before proved both jews and gentiles, that they are all under sin;
